reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the claim that O and N impurities promote phase segregation and softening in TiVNbTa upon aging at 700°C, but it does not provide data at 1273 K, nor does it demonstrate that impurity reduction actually preserves strength at that temperature. The hypothesis extrapolates the mechanism to a much higher temperature and assumes a substantial strength improvement without direct supporting evidence.
premises: Trace oxygen and nitrogen impurities in TiVNbTa promote phase segregation during thermal aging
Phase segregation depletes solute interstitials from the matrix, causing progressive softening
Reducing O and N impurities will suppress high-temperature phase segregation
Suppressing segregation preserves solid solution strengthening and prevents formation of weaker secondary phases
The purified alloy will retain substantially higher yield strength at 1273 K than the reported 330 MPa
